name: Green liberalism
summary: Green liberalism, as Marcel Wissenburg coined and set it out in 1998, holds that liberalism can absorb green concerns without treating nature as valuable in itself: equal citizenship, fairness and liberty to follow one's own plan of life allow, and even prescribe, environmentally benign behaviour. It rejects absolute property rights, accepts a restraint principle against destroying goods unless unavoidable, extends moral concern to some animals, but rules out population control as incompatible with liberty and refuses to prescribe one ecological way of life.
scope: The strand Wissenburg named in Green Liberalism: The Free and the Green Society (1998) and developed in his later chapters and articles, as the defining sources (his own texts, Arias-Maldonado's scholarship, and a 2020 essay on the term) describe it. Party platforms (the Swiss Green Liberal Party, the UK Liberal Ecology Group) are other subjects: their programmes are not used for answers. It excludes eco-socialist and deep-ecology strands, which Wissenburg treats as its rivals.

missingStatements.text: Destroying natural resources should require compensation.
missingStatements.rationale: Wissenburg's restraint principle, central to his green liberalism, demands exactly this limit on the freedom to destroy.

notes: Rebuilt in a later pass under rules 7. The earlier pass leaned on Wikipedia and on the Swiss Green Liberal Party's platform; those answers are nulled with their history kept, as are answers deduced from general liberal values (equal citizenship, liberty, liberal democracy), which do not settle specific statements. Themes searched: property, population, nature's value, animals, future generations, neutrality and lifestyles, markets and free-market environmentalism, democracy, borders and global justice (Wissenburg's own chapters), scholarship on his work. Wissenburg's texts stay at the level of principle and say nothing on taxes, energy, technology, welfare or most cultural questions, so most statements are null and the profile may fail the uncertainty rule; that is the honest result.
